published paper in authors institutional repository

claims.claim: Striped coats reduced horsefly landings relative to uniform coats.
claims.conditions: 7 domestic horses, three commercial coats worn in randomized order; materials were not standardized.
claims.notClaimed: all flies, total protection or a universal effect size

claims.claim: Approaching flies failed to decelerate normally near zebra pelage in study videos.
claims.conditions: 2019 sampled captive animals; animation is explanatory, not measured tracks.
claims.notClaimed: known neural illusion or every trajectory

claims.claim: Checked patterns can reduce landings; parallel stripes are not required.
claims.location: Abstract and results comparing striped, checked and grey coats
claims.notClaimed: all check patterns repel all insects

claims.claim: High contrast stripes deterred landings more effectively than lightly contrasting stripes in the study.
claims.conditions: identically arranged coat patterns with varied contrast
claims.notClaimed: human visual contrast equals fly perception

claims.claim: Small dark patches are a proposed explanation; the full visual mechanism remains unresolved.
claims.conditions: hypothesis rather than definitive neural mechanism
